title: Insalata di Mare
subtitle: Italian seafood salad with squid, prawns, and mussels in lemon and olive oil
excerpt: Insalata di mare is a cold Italian seafood salad of cooked squid, prawns, and mussels dressed with extra-virgin olive oil, lemon juice, parsley, and garlic. It is a staple of Italian coastal restaurants and a summer antipasto that can be prepared a day ahead and refrigerated until needed.
sourceNotes: Insalata di frutti di mare is documented throughout Italian coastal cooking. Artusi, La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene (1891), public domain, includes various cold seafood preparations. The salad format with olive oil and lemon is a coastal Italian standard.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dressed seafood improves with 1 to 4 hours of marinating in the fridge. Do not add the parsley until ready to serve.

content.text: Insalata di mare uses the three most common Italian coastal seafood items: squid, prawns, and mussels. Each is cooked separately and for a different time, then combined warm in the dressing so the marinade penetrates as they cool. The squid is the trickiest: it must be cooked either very briefly (under 2 minutes) or for a long time (over 30 minutes); anything between produces rubber.

items.prepNote: cleaned, bodies cut into 1 cm rings, tentacles left whole

content.text: Open the {{mussels}} of mussels: place them in a wide saucepan with {{white-wine-dry}} of white wine over a high heat, cover, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until all the mussels have opened. Discard any that remain closed. Remove from the shells, set the mussel meat aside, and strain the cooking liquid through a fine sieve.

Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil. Cook {{squid}} of squid rings and tentacles for 45 to 60 seconds until just opaque. Remove with a slotted spoon. In the same boiling water, cook {{prawns-raw}} of prawns for 2 to 3 minutes until pink and firm. Drain.

Whisk together {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} of olive oil, the juice of {{lemon}} lemon, {{garlic}} of grated garlic, {{salt-table}} of salt, and {{black-pepper}} of pepper in a large bowl. Add the chilli flakes if using. Toss the still-warm squid, prawns, and mussels in the dressing. Leave to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Stir in {{parsley-flat}} of chopped parsley just before serving. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve at cool room temperature, not fridge-cold.

items.cause: The squid was cooked too long. Squid has a narrow window: under 2 minutes it is tender, over 2 minutes it toughens, and only after 30 or more minutes of slow cooking does it soften again.
items.fix: Boil squid rings for no more than 1 minute. Remove as soon as they are just opaque and white through.

items.cause: Too little dressing, or the seafood was dressed when cold rather than warm.
items.fix: Dress the seafood while still warm so the oil and lemon penetrate. Taste and adjust the seasoning after chilling , cold food needs more salt than warm food.

content.text: Insalata di mare is a staple of Italian coastal restaurants from Venice to Palermo. The seafood varies by region: clams in Campania, spider crab in Venice, octopus in Sicily. The principle is the same everywhere. Poach or steam the seafood, then dress it while warm with good olive oil and lemon. Serve at cool room temperature, not fridge-cold. A calamari-only version is common in some regions.
